title: Calculus intuition: accumulate, optimize, and undo

turns.message: Give me a challenge on this.
I’ll guess: a negative rate still adds positive area to the accumulated amount.
I’m stuck; how do I include the starting volume in an accumulation problem?
Give me another challenge on this.
Correct answer: signed area is net change, so add the initial amount separately; a negative rate makes the amount fall.
/verify The derivative of a continuous accumulation function equals the current rate at the moving boundary.

expectations.notes: Distinguish net change from final amount and report the requested quantity; connect a rate graph to signed rectangles and the FTC; mention the chain factor when the accumulation limit is itself a function.
